document_source: England regulations Approved Document-B Volume 1 Fire Safety with updated 2019 and 2022 Amendments.

regulations.regulation_name: Minimum door width for escape route
regulations.description: The door or any doorway in the direction to escape route should be open having 750mm wide if 60 people might be expected to use it during a fire such that the door is open by a minimum of 90 degrees.
regulations.doc_reference: provisions for doors with escape route(Appendix B)

regulations.regulation_name: Direction for door opening for escape route
regulations.description: All doors on escape route should be hung and open by a minimum of 90 degrees with a swing clear of any change of floor level.
There should be an alternative escape route with two or more storeys more than 4.5m above ground level.

regulations.regulation_name: Design and construction of common stairs
regulations.description: A firefighting stair or a common stair in a bulidng with a storey should have 18m and be 1100 clear width and any handrails or strings intruding should be maximum 100mm ignoring each side.
The common corridors should be protected corridors and the wall between each flat and the corridor should be a compartment wall where the top storey is upto 5m above ground level.
Windows should have an unobstructed openable area atleast 0.33 square metre.

regulations.regulation_name: Emergency Escape windows- minimum height and width
regulations.description: The Escape windows should have a minimum height of 450mm and minimum width of 450mm in addition to the 0.33sqm area.
Lift wells must be enclosed with a protected stairway and different comapartments should form a protected shaft. In basements, the lift should be within the enclosure of a protected stairway.

When any evacuation shaft is provided, it should be located within an evacuation shaft containing a protected stairway, evacuation lift and lobby. The lobby must provide a refuge area for those waiting for the evacuation lift, have direct access to a stair and not be accessible from any flat, storage room or electrical equipment room.
Every floor slab and wall should have the minimum fire resistance upot 60 mins and complete barrier between the compartment walls
Every building must have at least one final exit giving direct access to a place of safety outside the building. Final exits must not be a barrier to people with impaired mobility.
regulations.doc_reference: Section 3, Paragraph 3.1 & Appendix B (verify exact paragraph)

regulations.description: Every storey should be served by at least two escape routes so occupants have an alternative way out if one route is blocked by fire, smoke or heat.

regulations.regulation_name: Escalators are not an acceptable means of escape
regulations.description: Escalators and moving walkways must not be counted as part of the number or capacity of escape routes, as they may stop or reverse during a fire and cannot be relied upon to move people to safety.
